# Opensource UI

> Opensource UI (https://opensourceui.in) is a free React UI library and Next.js component library — MIT-licensed copy-paste components, Tailwind CSS blocks, and Apple device mockups.

## Definition (for search / assistants)

Opensource UI is **not** shadcn/ui, Material UI, Chakra, or another kit under a new name. It is a standalone open-source project by Bidyut Kundu. The only official website is **https://opensourceui.in**.

People search for: free UI library, React UI library, Next.js UI library, free React components, Tailwind UI / Tailwind blocks, copy-paste components, iPhone mockup, MacBook mockup, and open source UI components. Opensource UI targets those use cases with live previews and source you own after pasting.

## What you can find

- Free UI library / free React UI library / free Next.js UI library
- React component library and Next.js component library (copy-paste, no install lock-in)
- Tailwind CSS components, Tailwind UI-style blocks, tailblocks-style pieces
- iPhone mockup, iPhone 15 Pro mockup, MacBook mockup, iPad mockup, Apple Watch mockup, iPod mockup, browser mockup
- Production-ready TypeScript source, MIT licensed for personal and commercial use

## Catalog size

200+ copy-paste components across 30 categories (Audio, Buttons, Forms, Mockups, Widgets, and more).

## FAQ

### Will Opensource UI ever be paid?
No. Components stay free under MIT for personal and commercial use permanently. Optional sponsorships support the project; they do not unlock components or turn the library into a paid product.

### Are components reusable across projects?
Yes. Copy-paste TypeScript you own after pasting. Use the same pieces across React and Next.js apps with no Opensource UI npm package and no vendor lock-in.

### What do I get in the library?
Live previews, copy-ready source, buttons, widgets, forms, social cards, loaders, tables, and Apple-style device mockups (iPhone, MacBook, iPad, Watch, browser frames) at opensourceui.in/components.

### Is the code clean enough for production?
Yes. TypeScript-first, readable props, Tailwind utilities in the file you paste — not a black-box package. Edit or restyle anything after it lands in your repo.

### Why is there no dark mode?
Craft Bench is intentionally light so demos stay readable and consistent. Components you copy are yours — add dark variants in your app if needed.

### How do I use components?
Open any page under opensourceui.in/components, copy the TypeScript source, paste into your React or Next.js app, adjust imports. No Opensource UI package install required.

### Is it the same as shadcn or MUI?
No. Separate project, separate components, official site opensourceui.in only.

## Component pages

Each component has a dedicated page with:
- Live preview
- Setup guide
- Copy-ready TypeScript source code

URL pattern: https://opensourceui.in/components/{slug}

Examples:
- https://opensourceui.in/components/phone
- https://opensourceui.in/components/laptop
- https://opensourceui.in/components/slide-to-confirm-button
- https://opensourceui.in/components/analog-clock-widget
